experiences.title: Aantaric Technologies Interview Experience|Analog Design Engineer|FTE|
experiences.full_content:
Eligibility

Only students from ECE, EE, and EI branches were eligible for the recruitment process.

Round 1: CGPA Shortlisting

The initial shortlisting was based on CGPA, with a minimum cutoff of 8.75. Students who met this criterion qualified for the next round.

Round 2: Test

Only 29 candidates were shortlisted for an 80-mark subjective test, divided into two sections:

Section 1 (30 marks): Focused on network theory.
Section 2 (50 marks): Covered analog and CMOS topics.
This test aimed to assess candidates' depth of understanding in fundamental electronics subjects.

Round 3: Interview

Only 3 candidates, including myself, advanced to the interview stage. Although conducted online, we were required to be physically present with a company representative.

Interview Questions:

High-Pass RC Circuit: I was asked to draw a high-pass RC circuit, derive its transfer function, and sketch the Bode magnitude and phase plots.
RC Circuit with Clock Pulse: Given a clock pulse applied to an RC circuit with RC significantly larger than the clock period (𝑇), I was asked to sketch the resulting waveform across the circuit.

Result

I was not selected for the next stage. Ultimately, only one candidate received the final offer.

experiences.full_content:
Hello Everyone,

My name is Shruti, and I recently completed my Bachelor's degree in Computer Science with a CGPA of 8.23. I am currently pursuing a Master's in Computer Applications in Pune. I am very passionate about problem-solving and have loved Java since my school days.

As we all know, Accenture is hiring for the SASA role. Basically, it is a non-technical role. A person who is pursuing a BCA or BSc is eligible for this role, or we can say any graduate with a three-year degree. The selection process is divided into three parts:

Online test
Communication test
Interview
Note: The online test, communication test, and interview will all influence your offer letter.

I took the online test, which was an aptitude test that anyone can easily crack. The second part is the communication test, in which you have to listen to audio and read the same sentences aloud.

Now, onto the final part: the interview. Here are some questions that the interviewer asked me:

Tell me about yourself.
What are your strengths?
Tell me about your projects.
How do you handle teamwork?
Have you participated in any cultural festivals?
Seniority-based questions.
This was the final question, and then it was over.

After 15 days, I received an email stating that they regretted to inform me that I was not selected. Maybe my preparation was not good at that time

And I think this is life you fail sometime to get something better. That was my first interview experience.

Hope you liked my first interview experience! See you soon.

experiences.title: Accenture Inerview Experience | Software Development | Full-time
experiences.full_content:
Preparing for a software development role at Accenture involves several steps and understanding the typical interview experience can be quite helpful. Here’s a general overview of what you might expect:

Application and Screening

Application Submission: Apply through Accenture's career portal or through a referral.
Initial Screening: You may receive a call from HR to discuss your resume, skills, and interest in the role. This is often a brief conversation to assess if you meet the basic qualifications.

Technical Assessment

Online Coding Test: You might be asked to complete an online coding test that assesses your problem-solving skills, algorithmic knowledge, and coding proficiency. Platforms like GeeksForGeeks, HackerRank or Codility are commonly used for these tests.
Technical Questions: Questions may cover data structures, algorithms, and programming languages relevant to the role.

Technical Interview

Coding Challenges: Expect to solve problems on a whiteboard or in an online coding environment. The focus will be on your approach, logic, and coding skills.
System Design: You might be asked to design a system or discuss architecture, focusing on scalability, reliability, and performance.

Behavioral Interview

STAR Method: Prepare to discuss past experiences using the STAR method (Situation, Task, Action, Result). Questions may cover teamwork, leadership, problem-solving, and project management.
Cultural Fit: Accenture places emphasis on cultural fit and alignment with their values, so be ready to discuss how you work in teams and handle challenges.

Final Interview

Managerial Round: This may involve a discussion with a senior manager or director, focusing on your fit for the role, career aspirations, and how you handle complex scenarios.
Project Discussion: You might discuss specific projects from your past, highlighting your contributions, challenges faced, and outcomes.
Offer and Negotiation
Offer Letter: If successful, you'll receive an offer letter detailing the role, compensation, and other benefits.
Negotiation: You can discuss terms, compensation, and other considerations before accepting the offer.

Preparation Tips:

Review Technical Skills: Brush up on coding, algorithms, and system design.
Study Accenture’s Values: Understand their core values and how they align with your career goals.
Practice Behavioral Questions: Prepare for common behavioral questions using reallife examples.
Research Projects: Familiarize yourself with Accenture’s projects and initiatives in the software development domain.
This outline should give you a good starting point for preparing for a software development role at Accenture.

experiences.title: Accenture Interview Experience
experiences.full_content:
I recently interviewed for the Software Engineer position at Accenture, one of the world's leading consulting firms specializing in digital transformation and technology services. I am sharing my interview experience to contribute to the knowledge of others, helping them prepare for opportunities in competitive environments like Accenture.

Preparation

Before the interview, I dedicated significant time to honing my problem-solving skills, particularly in data structures and algorithms. I practiced on platforms like HackerRank and LeetCode to sharpen my coding skills and took online courses on system design to enhance my knowledge. Additionally, I participated in mock interviews and researched the work culture at Accenture, including expectations for their technical roles. These resources greatly boosted my confidence and technical abilities.

Interview Process

The interview process at Accenture was segmented into four rounds:

Round 1: Online Test on HackerRank

The first round involved an online test conducted through HackerRank, consisting of coding questions focused on data structures and algorithms. The test included two medium-difficulty coding problems with a limited time frame. This round assessed my understanding of concepts like arrays, dynamic programming, and sorting algorithms, along with multiple-choice questions on computer science basics.

Round 2: Technical Interview 1

The second round was primarily focused on problem-solving and coding. The interviewer presented two real-time coding problems: the first involved string manipulation, and the second was a recursion problem. For both problems, the interviewer asked about the time complexity of my solutions and requested optimizations for one of the initial answers. The discussion then shifted to theoretical questions regarding object-oriented programming and operating systems.

Round 3: Technical Interview 2

In the third round, the emphasis was on understanding system design and real-world applications. I was tasked with designing a simple, scalable web application with a basic structure. I explained how I would handle certain edge cases in a distributed system. Towards the end of this round, I was asked about my previous projects and how they aligned with the work conducted at Accenture.

Round 4: HR Interview

The final round was an HR interview focused on behavioral questions to assess my fit within Accenture's culture. The HR representative inquired about my long-term career goals, how I handle pressure, and my contributions to previous teams. They also explored my adaptability to diverse environments, my communication skills with various nationalities, and my flexibility in a client-centric organization. It was clear that Accenture values a positive attitude and alignment with their core values of innovation, teamwork, and client satisfaction.

Challenges

One of the most significant challenges I faced was during the system design round, where I needed to think on my feet and present a clear solution for scalable architecture. The time constraints and real-time coding added complexity, but my mock interview practice helped manage my nerves.

Key Learnings

The interview process at Accenture is rigorous, emphasizing the importance of thorough preparation. While mastering core concepts in computer science, data structures, and algorithms is essential, articulating your thought process during problem-solving is equally important. The interviews are not just about solving problems but also about demonstrating teamwork and resilience in real-world scenarios.

For those preparing for similar interviews, I recommend focusing on both technical and soft skills. Ensure you are proficient in system design, dedicate time to coding practice on platforms like LeetCode, and be prepared for behavioral questions that assess cultural fit. Mock interviews with experienced coders can also alleviate anxiety and enhance your readiness.

Conclusion

In retrospect, my interview experience at Accenture underscored the value of timely preparation for various situations. Interviews can be unpredictable, but a solid foundation in both technical and behavioral aspects can make a significant difference. Every experience contributes to personal growth, regardless of the outcome. I hope my journey is helpful to you, and I encourage you to stay motivated and take one small step at a time toward your goals. Every small step can lead to significant progress!

experiences.title: Accenture Interview Experience 2025 | On-Campus
experiences.full_content:
My On-Campus Interview Experience with Accenture

Around 1,400 students applied for Accenture during the on-campus placement drive, with the only prerequisite being a PAN card. Here's how my journey unfolded:

Round 1: Online Aptitude and Technical Test

The first round was a combination of aptitude and technical questions. It consisted of around 70-80 questions covering topics like verbal reasoning, cloud computing, computer networks, and general aptitude. After completing this round, I successfully cleared it and was redirected to the next stage—coding.

Round 2: Coding Round

In the coding round, we were given two relatively straightforward tasks:

Check if a given number is a prime number.

Given a string, return a new string formatted as the first character + length of the string + the last character. I completed these in about 3-4 minutes and cleared this round as well.

Round 3: Online Communication Test (Non-Elimination)

This round assessed communication skills through tasks like repeating sentences, speaking on a given topic for two minutes, and finding errors in sentences. It wasn’t an elimination round, so everyone moved on to the next stage.

Round 4: Interview

My interview was scheduled for 10:00 AM, but I joined at 9:45 AM and it began promptly at 9:46 AM. The interviewer started by asking me about my projects, which allowed me to briefly introduce myself and discuss my work. I highlighted my research projects, patents, and extracurricular activities. As the president of my college’s club, I shared my leadership experience and also mentioned my involvement in over 20 hackathons, including winning two of them. I further talked about mentoring students in the Atal Tinkering Labs.

The interview was conversational, with the interviewer smiling throughout. He asked a few random questions, and I responded thoughtfully. When given the opportunity to ask questions, I asked 3-4, showing my interest and curiosity. The interview lasted about 25-30 minutes.

Verdict: I wasn’t selected, although 265 students from my college were. While it was disappointing, I’ve learned that you can put in your best effort, but the final result isn’t always in your control. The key is to stay motivated and keep pushing forward!

experiences.title: Accenture Interview Experience
experiences.full_content:
I recently attended an interview with Accenture and wanted to share my experience to help others prepare for their interviews.

Interview Details

Duration: Approximately 10 minutes
Type: HR Interview (Although it was supposed to be a technical + HR interview, only the HR was present in my case)

Interview Process

1. Introduction

The interview began with a request to introduce myself. I provided a brief overview of my background, educational qualifications, and key skills.

2. Project Discussion

The interviewer asked about the project I had highlighted in my resume. I explained the project's objectives, technologies used, and my specific role in its development. The HR focused on understanding the challenges I faced during the project and how I overcame them, which gave me an opportunity to showcase my problem-solving abilities.

3. Greatest Achievement

Next, I was asked to share my greatest achievement. I chose an accomplishment that demonstrated my problem-solving skills and ability to work under pressure, aligning my response with Accenture's values of teamwork, innovation, and adaptability.

4. Questions for the Interviewer

At the end of the interview, the HR asked if I had any questions. I inquired about my potential job responsibilities, assuming I was selected. The HR provided a brief explanation of the roles and expectations, which helped me gain clarity about the position.

Key Takeaways

Preparation Matters: Even though it was an HR interview, I prepared for technical questions as well. This preparation boosted my confidence.
Clear and Concise Answers: Clarity in responses is essential, especially for short interviews.
Engagement Counts: Asking relevant questions shows your interest in the role and leaves a positive impression.

Final Thoughts

Though the interview was short and primarily focused on HR aspects, it was a positive experience. The HR was friendly and created a comfortable environment.

For those preparing for an Accenture interview, my advice is to:

Know your resume thoroughly and be ready to discuss your projects and achievements.
Prepare for technical and HR questions, even if the interview focuses on one area.
Stay calm and confident, and make sure to highlight your skills and accomplishments effectively.

Hi everyone! Today, I’m excited to share my interview experience with Accenture. Here's a detailed account of the process, from application to offer acceptance.

Application and Initial Contact

When I Applied: I submitted my application for a Java and Spring Boot developer role through the Naukri portal in May.
Initial Contact: A month later, in June, I received a call from Accenture. They asked about my:Technical skills
Total work experience
Current work location
Notice period

Shortly after, I was asked about my availability for an interview the following weekend, to which I confirmed my participation.

First Round: Technical Interview

The technical round was focused on Java and Spring Boot. The interviewer asked detailed questions, including:

Spring Boot Basics:What is Spring Boot, and how is it beneficial over the Spring framework?
What are Spring Boot actuators, and what are their uses?
Explain dependency injection and its significance.
Common annotations used in Spring Boot.

HTTP Methods:Differences between various HTTP methods.

Technical Concepts:How can we change the default port number in Spring Boot?
Difference between final, finally, and finalize keywords.
Difference between static and final methods.

Programming Task:Write a program to count the occurrence of characters in a string using HashMap.

The round lasted approximately 40 minutes. Shortly after, I received a call informing me that I had cleared the technical round and was shortlisted for the managerial round.

Second Round: Managerial Interview

The managerial round, conducted the following week, focused on my project experience and collaborative skills. Here’s a breakdown of the questions:

Project Details:Describe your role and responsibilities in your previous organization.
Which teams did you work closely with?
How do you approach new requirements?
Explain the design and documentation process for both backend and frontend.

Agile and Testing:How do you handle sprint cycles?
What is your approach to unit testing and its documentation?

Cloud Basics:Explain the differences between PaaS and SaaS.
How are these models used in Azure?

This round lasted 30 minutes and went smoothly. I was informed that I had cleared this round as well.

HR Discussion and Offer

A week later, I received a call from HR to discuss the offer. During this call, the HR representative explained the salary structure and shared the offer letter. I accepted the offer after carefully reviewing it.

Final Thoughts

The overall interview experience with Accenture was smooth and well-structured. The interviewers were professional, and the process allowed me to showcase both my technical and project management skills.

Good luck to everyone preparing for their interviews! Stay confident and be clear with your answers—it makes a world of difference.

experiences.title: Accenture Interview Experience| ASE & AASE
experiences.full_content:
Recently, Accenture visited our campus for recruitment for the ASE (Associate Software Engineer) and AASE (Advanced Associate Software Engineer) roles. Here's a detailed overview of the Cognitive and Technical assessment, as well as the coding round, which was conducted offline.

Assessment Overview:

We were notified about the assessment around 10 days before the actual test. The test was conducted in-person on campus, and we were required to give the assessment on our college's PCs with the webcam and audio on at all times. However, it didn’t seem like they were monitoring us very strictly.Two people from Accenture were present for supervision.

Round 1: Cognitive and Technical Assessment

The first round was a 90-minute test with 90 questions, and the questions were not divided into sections—all 90 were displayed at once.

Topics Covered:
Verbal Ability
Critical Reasoning
Abstract Reasoning
Networking, Security, and Cloud
MS Office and Common Applications
Pseudocode
Basic Software Engineering
The level of difficulty was fairly easy, so most students were able to qualify for the next round. Although the cutoff wasn’t disclosed, I estimate it to be around 55+ marks.

Round 2: Coding Assessment

After the cognitive and technical test, those who qualified moved on to the coding round. This round consisted of two coding questions, both of which were easy.

Question 1: Print All Prime Numbers up to a Given Number
You were required to take a number as input and print all the prime numbers from 2 to that number.
Example:
Input: 9
Output: 2 3 5 7

Question 2: Check if Two Strings are Misarranged Versions of Each Other
In this problem, you had to determine if two given strings are misarranged versions of the same string. Essentially, you had to check if the strings are anagrams.
Example:
Input: ab ba
Output: 1

You needed to return 1 or 0, not True or False. There were only 2 test cases provided, and while some students tried to hardcode the output using if-else statements, I wouldn't recommend doing this. Writing a generalized solution is always a safer approach.

Coding Environment and Tips:

The compiler provided by Accenture was not user-friendly, and many students found it challenging to work with. I highly suggest practicing with their mock tests to get familiar with the environment beforehand. Also, remember that you have to take input from the user manually during the exam.

Important Note: For the final exam, it’s mandatory to bring your original PAN card, so make sure to have it with you.

Pro Tip: From what we observed, there were only 3 unique coding questions that were being repeated across different students. If possible, try to coordinate with friends from earlier shifts to get an idea of the questions that may come your way.

experiences.title: Accenture Interview Experience | ASE | On-Campus
experiences.full_content:
Hello everyone,

I had the opportunity to interview for the ASE (Associate Software Engineer) role at Accenture. It was an on-campus opportunity. We had done our registration in July, 2023 and exams were scheduled in Aug - Sept, 2023. There were total 4 rounds:

Round 1 (Cognitive and Technical Assessment) & Round 2 (Coding Assessment):

This is an elimination round. Exam venue was our college lab and platform was SEB (Safe Exam Browser) - HirePro. Both rounds were on same day, only after qualifying in 1st round you will receive mail and link for 2nd round . The 1st round consisted of 90 ques, topics - Quantitative, English Ability, Reasoning, Pseudocode, Networking, Cloud, MS Office, and time allotted - 90 minutes. After completion, within 5-7 minutes results are on screen whether you are qualified or not, if qualified coding round will be activated.

Coding round consist of 2 ques, basically easy to medium. In my case 1st ques was from Dynamic programming, and 2nd was to find whether a number is lucky or not (if number contains 7 or 1 it is unlucky, if not, lucky).  After clearing this round, I received an email for the Communication Assessment round.

Round 3 (Communication Assessment):

This is not an elimination round. Every section has multiple questions, and each question are recorded means you will hear a voice and have to give answers orally. Contains 6 sections - Reading, Listening,  Jumbled Sentences, Questions and Answers, Listening and retelling same sentence /paragraph, Speaking on given topic (4-5 sentences), time allotted 30 minutes (approx). After, 2-3 days of completion of this round I received interview slot details.

Round 4(Interview):

(TR+HR) Questions were from resume and some situation based questions.

Introduce yourself
Project description
Any difficulties faced in project
Future scope of project
Apart from technical skills what did you learn from your internship
Your strength, weakness
Had any failure in life, how did you tackle that
Conflict based situational question
3 emerging technologies
Any ques for me (interviewer)
The interview was on 5th sept, 2023 and lasted for around 15-20 minutes. On 22-23rd sept, I received list of selected students from our college, and next day I also received LOI mail from Accenture, offer letter came in March and joining in June, 2024

experiences.title: Accenture Interview Experience | Associate Software Engineer (ASE)
experiences.full_content:
Accenture organized a pre-placement talk at our college in July 2024 for the role of Associate Software Engineer (ASE).

Round 1 (90 minutes) :

This was an aptitude round consisting of 90 multiple-choice questions with a time limit of 90 minutes. The questions covered general aptitude, MS Office, and computer fundamentals. It was an elimination round, with a cutoff ranging from 60% to 75%.

Round 2 (45 minutes):

Five minutes after completing the aptitude round, candidates received an email for the coding round. This round included two easy to medium-level coding questions with a time limit of 45 minutes. Candidates were allowed to use any programming language (C, C++, Java, .NET, Python, etc.). The questions were related to strings, stacks, arrays, and singly linked lists. To advance, it was recommended to solve at least one to one and a half questions.

Round 3 (25 minutes) :

This was a communication assessment conducted using Pearson's AI-powered application, with a time limit of 25 minutes. It included tasks such as storytelling, sentence repetition, and jumbled sentence exercises.

Round 4 (40 minutes) :

The interview round lasted about 40minutes. The interviewer began by asking me to introduce myself, followed by a brief discussion of my projects, certifications, and extracurricular activities. The interviewer then asked general managerial questions before moving on to technical questions related to object-oriented programming, DBMS, and Java (and other skills that I have mentioned in my resume). The interview concluded with an opportunity for me to ask questions.

Outcome: Selected.

experiences.title: Accenture Interview Experience for AASE Role (2024)
experiences.full_content:
Candidate Information

Status: Final-year student at MAIT IPU, currently placed in a company with a higher package than Accenture's AASE role.
Location: New Delhi, India
Interview Date: September 19, 2024

Overview of the Interview Process

1. Initial Screening

Duration: 30 minutes
Method: Online aptitude and coding test
Focus: Assessing general aptitude and basic programming skills.
Key Questions:Aptitude: Quantitative, Logical Reasoning
Coding Problems

Obstacles: None. The candidate successfully completed this round and moved on to the communication test.

2. Communication Test

Duration: 15 minutes
Method: Online recorded test.
Focus: Evaluating English proficiency, fluency, and clarity of communication.
Obstacles: None. Cleared successfully, and the candidate moved on to the interview slot selection.

3. Technical Round

Duration: Approximately 20-25 minutes (including interruptions).
Method: Online video interview via proprietary software.
Focus:Self-introduction
Project explanations
Questions about Accenture’s ongoing initiatives and areas of interest.

Key Questions:“Introduce yourself.”
“Explain any one of your projects.”
“Explain another project.”
“Do you have any questions for me?”

Obstacles:Technical Glitches: The interviewer’s video froze several times, and the meeting was exited twice due to network and power issues. The initial miscommunication about network problems was incorrectly blamed on the candidate.
Time Management: The interviewer’s rushed demeanor limited in-depth discussion or follow-up questions.
Proprietary Software Constraints: The candidate was unable to control the video call during the interview, which caused some difficulty in interacting during the session.

Post-Interview Reflections

Company Culture Insights

The interviewer seemed rushed and didn’t provide a structured introduction or feedback, making it difficult to gauge Accenture's work culture fully. This suggests the interviewer was possibly managing time constraints.

Work Environment

The proprietary software used for the interview had some reliability issues, affecting the overall experience. Technical glitches disrupted the interview flow, which could have impacted the candidate’s performance and overall perception of the company’s processes.

Benefits Highlight

There was no discussion regarding specific perks or benefits during the interview, which is typical unless the candidate specifically asks or moves to later stages of the hiring process.

Evaluator Feedback

The lack of follow-up questions or deeper engagement from the interviewer may indicate time constraints or a rushed process, which could affect how candidates feel about their interview experience.

Suggestions for Improvement

Technical Setup: Accenture should invest in ensuring that the proprietary software is reliable, user-friendly, and offers sufficient functionality to enhance the interview process.
Candidate Experience: Interviewers should follow a structured approach, beginning with an introduction, maintaining engagement throughout the interview, and providing clear feedback to candidates.
Communication: It’s crucial that candidates are not blamed prematurely for technical issues. Accenture should improve communication in case of connectivity problems.

Additional Information

After being kicked out of the meeting, the candidate rejoined and completed the interview when the interviewer returned. Despite the technical issues, the candidate remained professional and expressed interest in AI-related projects within Accenture, showing enthusiasm for innovation-driven roles.

Closing Note

Despite the technical difficulties and the interviewer’s rushed behavior, the candidate tried to maintain professionalism throughout the process. While the outcome is not dependent on this offer, the candidate noted that being rejected due to uncontrollable factors would be disheartening. The results are awaited and will be shared once released

experiences.full_content:
Accenture Visit to NIT Jamshedpur - September 2024

Accenture visited NIT Jamshedpur in September 2024 for the role of Advanced Application Engineer Analyst, offering a fixed pay of 11.89 LPA. All branches were eligible for the role, with a minimum requirement of 6.5 CGPA and 65% in both 10th and 12th grades.

Selection Process

The selection process consisted of four rounds:

Cognitive and Technical Assessment
Coding Assessment
Communication Assessment (Non-Elimination)
Technical + HR Interview
Final selection at Accenture is based on the overall evaluation of all four rounds. The Cognitive and Technical Assessment is scored out of 90 marks with no negative marking. The Coding Assessment included two easy to medium-level questions: the first worth 10 marks and the second worth 20 marks. The marks for the Communication Assessment and interview are not disclosed by Accenture but are included in the overall evaluation.

Cognitive and Technical Assessment - 26th September

This elimination round consisted of six sections, with a total of 90 questions to be solved in 90 minutes. To pass, candidates must meet an unknown sectional cutoff set by Accenture. This round tested English ability, reasoning, MS Office skills, pseudo code in Python, networking security, and cloud concepts.

Approximately 220 students participated in this test.

Tip: The pseudo code section was time-consuming due to many questions involving bit manipulation operations, so ensure you allocate enough time for this section.

Most candidates found passing this round manageable, but the scores had a significant impact on overall selection. Results were displayed on the test screen within 5-10 minutes, after which we proceeded to the Coding Assessment.

Around 170 students advanced to the Coding Assessment.

Coding Assessment - 26th September

The Coding Assessment consisted of two questions to be solved in 45 minutes. The first question involved easy string manipulation, while the second focused on the concept of a monotonic stack, similar to the well-known "next greater element" problem.

I solved both questions optimally in 20 minutes.

Tip: Aim to solve both questions in the most optimal way, as graded test cases are used, and marks are awarded based on the optimality of the solution.

Only those who solved both problems were shortlisted for the next round, with 17 students moving on to the Communication Assessment.

Communication Assessment - 30th September

All shortlisted candidates received an email for the Communication Assessment, which had a 24-hour window for completion. It consisted of 6-7 sections, including read and speak, listen to audio and speak, and speaking on a particular topic. AI evaluated our communication skills.

Tip: Although this round was non-eliminating, it was crucial for the overall evaluation. Ensure you complete this round sincerely in a quiet environment with a stable internet connection.

On 3rd October, we received an email to choose our interview slots scheduled for 4th October.

Technical + HR Interview - 4th October

The interview at Accenture was primarily HR-focused, but candidates should also prepare their technical responses. My interview began at 12:30 PM and lasted for 25 minutes. The following questions were asked:

Introduction - Prepare your introduction beforehand and practice well.
Explain your internship (if any), group projects (if any), and individual projects - speak smoothly.
What was your role in the group project?
What challenges did you face while working on the project? What was the team size, and did you have any conflicts with team members? How did you handle them?
Do you prefer working in a team or individually? What differences have you noticed between the two?
What feedback did you receive from your team members after working together?
What is the difference between an array and a linked list?
How would you rate yourself in Data Structures, Algorithms, and Object-Oriented Programming?
Can you implement a queue using a stack? (I explained the logic using OOP methods.)
What is data abstraction? (Always explain with real-life examples.)
Suppose you are a team lead; how would you distribute a project among your team members?
Have you completed any certifications beyond your academics?
Do you have any questions for me? - This is crucial for ending your interview positively. I asked three thoughtful questions related to challenges faced in IT and expectations from freshers, which impressed the interviewer.
Tip: The first and last five minutes of your interview are critical for making a strong impression. Stay calm, take a few seconds to think before answering HR questions.

Final Selection

I waited 12 days for the results, and on the morning of 16th October, we received a list from our TAP cell indicating that six students were selected for the full-time role, with me being at the top of the list.

experiences.title: Accenture Interview Experience for Advance Application Engineering (AEH) - On-Campus -  FTE - 2025
experiences.full_content:
In late August 2024, Accenture visited our campus to recruit Full-Time Employees (FTE) for the role of AEH, starting in 2025. The application process was open to all branches, and it saw an overwhelming response, with over 6,000 students applying for the online assessment.

The recruitment process consisted of four rounds, each serving as an elimination round, except for the communication assessment. These rounds included:

1. Online Assessment

2. Coding Round

3. Communication Assessment

4. Technical + HR Interview

Round 1: Cognitive and Technical MCQ Assessment

The first round tested our aptitude and logical reasoning skills. We were required to wear formal attire and report to the designated rooms assigned by the Career Development Centre.

This round consisted of six sections, and we had to answer a total of 90 questions within 90 minutes. The topics covered were diverse, ranging from Quantitative Aptitude, Verbal Reasoning and Logical Reasoning to Pseudocode, Networking & Cloud, and MS Office.

The difficulty level varied from easy to medium. Once the assessment was completed, the results were announced almost instantly—within two minutes. Candidates who cleared this round moved on to the coding section, while others received a message indicating they had not been selected.

Important Points:

- Difficulty Level: Easy to Medium

- Topics Covered: Quantitative Aptitude, Verbal, Logical Reasoning, Pseudocode, Networking & Cloud, MS Office.

- Note: This was an elimination round with no negative marking.

Round 2: Coding Round

The second round was a coding challenge designed to test our problem-solving and programming skills. The duration was 45 minutes, during which we were required to solve two questions. The difficulty level ranged from easy to medium.

To advance to the next round, it was essential to solve both questions. Only candidates who performed well in this round moved on to the Communication Assessment.

Out of the 6,500 students who initially applied, only 650 were selected for the next stage.

Important Points:

- Duration: 45 minutes

- Number of Questions: 2

- Difficulty Level: Easy to Medium

- Note: This was an elimination round, so performing well was crucial for further progression.

Round 3: Communication Round

Each candidate selected for this round received further details via email. This was an AI-based assessment that evaluated our communication skills. The round consisted of six different sections, each with a set number of questions and varying time limits. Candidates had a 24-hour window to complete the test at their convenience.

The six sections included:

1. Reading Sentences – 8 Questions

2. Repeating Sentences – 16 Questions

3. Questions and Answers – 24 Questions

4. Sentence Building – 10 Questions

5. Story Retelling – 3 Questions

6. Speak on a Given Topic – 2 Questions

The total duration for this assessment was 30 minutes.

Important Points:

- Note: This is not an elimination round, but it is recommended to perform your best as it contributes to the overall evaluation.

- Tips:

- Use wired headsets with a good-quality microphone (avoid Bluetooth devices).

- Take the test in a quiet environment with a stable internet connection to avoid interruptions.

Round 4: Technical + HR Interview

This round lasted around 25 to 30 minutes. Candidates received the interview date and were given the option to choose a time slot that suited them.

The interview began with a brief introduction from the interviewer, followed by the classic "Tell me about yourself" question. The discussion then moved on to various topics, including:

- Academic Journey: What you have accomplished over the past 3.5 years in college.

- Project Discussion: Deep dive into projects mentioned on the resume.

- Group Project and Leadership Experience: Roles and responsibilities in group projects.

- Internship Experience: Details and learnings from the internship.

- Hackathon Participation: Experiences and outcomes from hackathons.

- Handling Failures: Situations where you encountered failure and how you dealt with them.

- Skill Development: The most important skills developed during project creation and where they were applied further.

- Open Questions: The interviewer asked if I had any questions for him (Tip: Always ask a couple of thoughtful questions. This shows your interest and helps you connect better with the interviewer).

Tips for this Round:

- Stay confident and calm while answering questions.

- Read through various interview experiences beforehand to prepare for potential questions.

- When the interviewer asks if you have any questions for them, always try to ask at least one or two thoughtful questions. This leaves a positive impression.

After about 10 days, our Career Development Centre announced the final list of selected candidates. I was overjoyed and proud to find my name among those who made it. It was a moment of immense satisfaction, knowing that all the hard work and preparation had paid off!

experiences.full_content:
Accenture visited our campus, Vellore Institute of Technology (VIT), for the 2025 pass-out batch, offering a Super Dream full-time role as an Advanced App Engineering Analyst. Nearly all eligible students were permitted to take the test, with around 3,300 students from all four VIT campuses participating.

Eligibility Criteria: All branches, CGPA of 6.5+, Minimum 65% in board exams

Round 01: Online Assessment (Aptitude + Coding):

The first round consisted of two sections: Aptitude and Coding.

Aptitude Section:

The aptitude test covered five key domains:

Verbal Ability, MS Office, Cloud and Networking, Logical Reasoning, Others.

The difficulty level was moderate, and thorough preparation is crucial. It’s important to score above the cutoff in this section to qualify for the coding round. After submitting the aptitude test, your result is displayed immediately, and if you clear the cutoff, you can proceed directly to the coding round.

Coding Section:

The coding round featured two questions:

First question: A simple problem where you had to check if a dice roll is even, and based on that, print specific outputs. (The exact logic was straightforward, though I don’t recall all the details.)

Second question: This was more complex. Given two numbers, you had to:

Find all prime numbers between those two numbers.

For each prime number, check whether all its rotations (cyclic permutations of its digits) are also prime.

If all rotations of a prime number are prime, add that number to a cumulative sum.

Finally, return the sum of all such prime numbers that meet the condition.

The first question was easy, while the second was medium to hard in difficulty, requiring a deeper understanding of prime numbers and cyclic permutations.

Note for us test were taken for 3 days and each day three slots and for me it was second day and second slot.

Most Important Note for the Coding Assessment: They did not display all the test cases during the exam. Only after full submission were the hidden test cases evaluated. It’s up to you to anticipate which test cases your code might fail. Many of my friends passed the visible test cases for both questions and believed they had solved them correctly. However, they didn’t receive a call for the next round because their solutions didn’t account for the hidden test cases.

.You will receive your result immediately after the exam, letting you know whether you’ve qualified for the next round or not.

After three days we received shortlist around 600-650 people got shortlisted for next round.

Round 02: Communication Assessment:

This round was a non-elimination round but was made compulsory, It consisted of speaking and listening tests. You can refer to YouTube videos for that.

Round 03: Technical + HR:

It was quite a rollercoaster! My interview was scheduled for the 10:30 AM slot, but I ended up waiting in the queue until 2:30 PM—over four hours! Most of the other candidates had completed their interviews long before mine, which made me anxious. Finally, my turn came, and here’s how it went:

Questions:

Introduce yourself.

Explain your favorite project.

If you were to do this project again, would you do anything differently?

Tell me about your internship experience.

How was your experience working with the client during your internship?

How would you handle a team conflict?

How do you manage deadlines?

What is your least favorite subject?

Lastly, do you have any questions for us?

These were the questions they asked during the interview.

Note: The interview primarily focused communication skills, English fluency and on how well I can manage and interact with clients, which were the key assessment points.

After 10 days, we received the list of shortlisted students. Out of 600 candidates, 150 were offered full-time positions—and I was one of them! :)

VERDICT: SELECTED

experiences.title: Accenture Interview Experience for ASE and AASE (On-Campus || Batch : 2025)
experiences.full_content:
I applied for a position at Accenture through my college's on-campus placement drive. The recruitment process consisted of four rounds. I was informed about the opportunity on July 26, 2024, and filled out the necessary application. When completing the application, you'll need to select three preferred job locations, so be sure to consider your preferences beforehand. Additionally, a PAN card is a mandatory requirement for participating in the exam.

This is how my TIMELINE looks.

Registration: 26 Jul 2024
1st Round: 28 Aug, 2024
2nd Round: 28 Aug, 2024
3rd Round: 31 Aug, 2024
4th Round: 5 Sep, 2024
Results: 28 Sep, 2024

1st Round: Cognitive and Technical Assessment—MCQ Test (90 Questions—90 min):

The initial stage of the Accenture recruitment process is a cognitive and technical assessment, conducted on-campus in our college's computer labs. This round is relatively straightforward as it doesn't include any quantitative aptitude questions.

The assessment consists of 90 questions divided into six sections, and you'll have 90 minutes to complete it. You can freely move between different sections. To pass this round, you need to achieve a minimum score of 75% (subject to potential adjustments based on the final cutoff).

English Ability(Verbal) - 17 Ques
Critical Reasoning and Problem Solving - 18 Ques
Abstract Reasoning - 15 Ques
Common Application and MS Office - 12 Ques
Pseudo Code - 18 Ques
Fundamentals of Networking, Security, and Cloud - 10 Ques

2nd Round: Coding Test (2 Questions – 45 min):

If you successfully pass the first round, you'll proceed to the coding round on the same day.

This test consists of two questions, typically categorized as easy or medium difficulty. You'll have 45 minutes to complete the test, and the difficulty level can vary. It's common for the first question to be easy, while the second question may be more challenging. To clear this round, you need to solve at least one of the questions.

I recommend searching for previous year Accenture coding questions, as many of them tend to be repeated.

I was given the following coding questions :  Accenture Coding Question

3rd Round: Communication Assessment:

After successfully passing the coding round, you'll be required to participate in the Communication Assessment round. This round is not eliminatory, but it's mandatory. You'll have 2-3 days to complete it.

Communication Assessment Breakdown

Reading: Read aloud with proper punctuation (8 questions)
Repeat: Repeat sentences exactly as heard (16 questions)
Questions: Answer questions based on prompts (24 questions)
Sentence Builds: Rearrange words to form sentences (10 questions)
Story Retellings: Retell brief stories (3 questions)
Open Questions: Speak on given topics (2 questions)
TIPS:

Watch Youtube videos to familiarize yourself with the assessment format. Find a quiet space and ensure your headphones are working properly. Consider taking the exam at night for optimal focus.

4th Round: Interview (Online):

First, you'll need to book a time slot that suits you for the interview. If the interview starts late, don't worry—just wait patiently in the virtual interview lobby.

Accenture typically focuses on project-related questions along with HR questions, so it's important to have a deep understanding of your projects and be prepared for some common HR questions.

My interview was scheduled for 5th September 2024 at 11:00 AM. I entered the lobby at 10:45 AM, and the interviewer joined at 11:02 AM. He introduced himself and then began asking questions, starting with:

Introduce yourself.
Tell me about your project.
Follow-up questions on the project.
At the end, he asked if I had any questions, and I asked him two: one about the technologies extensively used at Accenture, and the other about his experience working there. The interview was quite brief, lasting only about 7 minutes.

Results :

Accenture was hiring for two profiles:

Associate Software Engineer (ASE)
Advanced Associate Software Engineer (AASE).
I got selected for the Associate Software Engineer (ASE) profile.

I received the list of selected students from the TNP cell on 28th September, and on 30th September, I received the congratulations email. Out of 405 students who attended the first round and 105 who were interviewed, only 34 were selected.

VERDICT : SELECTED

experiences.title: Accenture Interview Experience for ASE | On-campus
experiences.full_content:
Accenture visited our campus offering two exciting roles: Associate Software Engineer (ASE) with a package of 4.5 LPA, and Advanced Associate Software Engineer (AASE) with 6.5 LPA. Both positions followed the same hiring process.

Hiring Process

Accenture generally has 4 rounds all are elimination rounds except the communication round,

Cognitive and Technical Assessment. (Aptitude, analytical and logical thinking, English ability, pseudocode, technical MCQs)
Coding Round.
Communication round.
Virtual Interview.

Round 1: Cognitive and Technical Assessment

I had my first round on August 28, about a month after applying. The admit card was received two days prior. The test consisted of 90 MCQs in 90 minutes, divided into two main sections:

Cognitive Section: English ability, logical reasoning, and abstract reasoning with about 50 questions.
Technical Section: 18 pseudocode questions, 12 scenario-based Microsoft questions, and 10 scenario-based networking and security questions, totaling around 40 questions.
Pay special attention to the pseudocode questions as they can be time-consuming. Good practice and solving mock tests beforehand are extremely helpful. Overall, the difficulty was easy to moderate, and about 70% of students advanced to the next round. After completing both sections, the results were displayed after a 10-15 minute wait. Those who cleared the cutoff were immediately invited to the coding round, which took place the same day.

Prepare well for this round, as some questions can be tricky and time-consuming. I recommend solving at least 4-5 mock tests within the allotted time to be ready.

Round 2: Coding round

You have 2 Coding questions, 45 Minutes. In my case both the coding questions were easy. You should be good in basic programming and logic, Basic concepts like maths, arrays, loops, counting, maps, and strings will be enough. My first question was, 2 strings were given and you have to calculate the difference between no. of spaces in both. and state whether they are odd or even along with diff (e.g. Even4, Odd7). I did this in Javascript.

My second question was a moderate level where I was given an array of temperatures. and you have to find the longest monotonically decreasing subarray's length. I was easy too. and solved both the question. One who is slightly active on coding platform, will help you to get this round.

Round 3: Communication Round

It was virtual, non elimination round. I received communication round link after 2-3 days after Round 2. It was easy. You will have 3-4 sections

Read the sentence on screen.
Listen the sentence carefully and repeat.
Listen the story and answer the question, note the keywords.
You will be asked to give 45 second speech on random topic, with 30 minutes to think.
Even though its non-elimination round be serious, take this test at quiet place, use good quality headphones. Even slight background noise can make you to reappear the test, be clear and loud in speaking.

Round 4: Interview Round(Technical+ HR)

After a week on 5th sept, my interview was scheduled. You will receive slot confirmation, like a day before. Here i faced the problem, my interviewer didn't appeared for whole day. I was waiting in online call for whole day, but no one came. I was disappointed and raised a Ticket and reported TnP. Many of my friends, faced this issue of waiting in queue.

Fortunately, within a week Accenture rescheduled the interview of those who faced issue. This time I was calm, my interviewer was also good. He asked me few questions like

Introduce Yourself, education, skills, family, certifications etc.
About Projects.
Discussed about Hackathons and Team related questions.
Why particular Tech Stack.
How do you build network.
Questions related to Certifications.
Basic questions related to Accenture, why Accenture.
Ask any questions
For this round, be honest and confident. Prepare thoroughly, especially with scenario-based questions. While the interview focused more on communication and behavior than technical depth, it’s important to stay calm and composed.

Final Verdict: After 1 month of wait, I got selected.

experiences.full_content:
The recruitment process for Accenture includes certain steps:

Cognitive Ability and Technical assessment & Coding assessment
Communication Assessment
Interview

Cognitive Ability and Technical Assessment & Coding Assessment

This assessment has 6 sections:

English Ability
Critical Reasoning and Problem Solving
Abstract Reasoning
Common Application and MS Office
Pseudo Code
Networking Security and Cloud
Each section has MCQs with no negative marking and the time allotted is 90 mins.

The coding Assessment has 2 Questions and the time allotted is 45 mins.

Languages you can use:

C
C++
Dot Net
Java
Python
To clear the coding assessment, you must successfully run and compile at least one question on every test case.

Communication assessment

This assessment is to test the candidate's Communication Skills. This round is not an elimination round mostly all candidates clear this round.

Tips:

Speak Clearly
Speak like you are talking to a person
Use your regular accent
Listen Carefully
Use Good Quality earphones
Choose a quiet place with no background noise

Interview

There was only one interviewer, making it a one-on-one interview. It felt more like an HR interview, as most of the questions were behavioral. The questions I was asked and the answers I gave are:

>>Tell me about yourself:

Mention your name, college, passing year, and cgpa, try to add your achievements if any, Then add your academics work like projects(name, and its work), college fests participations, languages you learnt, Any courses, and extracurriculars.

>>Are you planning to go for Mtech or job

As I have told my gate score in my introduction so i was asked this question.

>>Extra Skill other than technical and academic

You can tell your hobby like playing any instrument or any sports, and something you achieved in that like , I said "I play chess and I was winner at district level chess competition".

>>Tell me more about Your project

Start by explaining your project name, tell if it was individual or group project, if group project what was your role and what particular language you have worked on, tell how you contributed in that project.

>>So you were given this project by someone or it was your idea

If it was your idea tell why you chose this project and its uses what problem it solves etc.

>>What all languages you used in project ?

>>What work you have done in your project ?

>>What issues you faced while making this project ?

Try to tell issues which does not impact your learning, like don't say I don't know how to code etc. Rather you can say the frontend designing was a issue as everything have to be user friendly or database designing was tough so that in future any modifications can be done easily, or dividing the work among team members according to their skills.

>>What was your mentor reaction to your project what were there suggestions ?

Try to tell positive feedbacks of your project.

>>What is your favourite subject and why ?

Tell the subject from your engineering field so that you can describe it well.

>>Tell some of your Achievements

>>Where you see yourself in upcoming years ?

Try to tell something you would like learn like "I see myself as a expert in ", I want to see myself as leading a project, I want to learn more, and apply my learnings. I would like to broaden my network of industrial contacts.

>>Is it your first interview ?

>>Do you know any cloud technology ?

>>Why we should hire you ?

Tell how you can be useful for their company, tell how well you can manage the work load, add your strengths like good team leader add example where you have lead a team, fast learner give example where you have learnt something very fast for some presentation etc.

>>Do you have any questions ?

Always ask 2-3 questions this will show that you are interested in joining.

Questions that you can ask:

Will there be any training period ?
Any prerequisite or any skill I should learn before joining ?
What Will be my particular work ?
Is there any suggestion you would like to give so that i can improve myself ?
Will there be any bond ?
Tips:

Try to be calm don't panic interviewer is just another person.
Don't give too long answers try to short and precise.
Listen to the question carefully if you didn't understand ask to repeat.
And if you don't know the answer don't sit ideal, You can say "Right now i don't know the answer but i will definitely learn about it".
Whether you secure the job or not, every interview is an opportunity to grow. Embrace the process, learn from it, and use each experience to better prepare for the next challenge.

ALL THE BEST !! FOR YOUR INTERVIEW..

experiences.title: Accenture Interview Experience for Associate Software Engineer role (ASE)
experiences.full_content:
Here's a detailed account of my interview process with Accenture, covering every stage from initial screening to the HR interview.

Screening Process

The initial screening served as a basic filter to ensure I met the required academic qualifications and graduation year.

Key Tip: Having a well-structured resume that highlights your skills and projects effectively is essential.
Timeline: This stage typically occurs about a month before the interview rounds.

Round 1: Cognitive and Technical Assessment

This round tested reasoning, verbal ability, and basic programming concepts.

Key Topics to Study

Reasoning: Logical puzzles, pattern recognition, seating arrangements.
Verbal Ability: Grammar, sentence correction, reading comprehension.
Technical: Programming basics, including loops, arrays, and object-oriented programming (OOP).

Resources I Used

Reasoning and Verbal: RS Aggarwal and mock tests on IndiaBix.
Technical Concepts: GeeksforGeeks (GFG) Programming Basics section.

Round 2: Coding Round

This round involved two coding problems, ranging from easy to moderately challenging, aimed at testing problem-solving and algorithmic thinking.

Key Topics to Focus On

Arrays, Strings, and Loops.
Sorting algorithms (Bubble Sort, Selection Sort).
Basic data structures (Stacks, Queues).

Recommended Resources

GFG DSA Self-Paced Course for a structured approach.
Practice platforms like HackerRank and LeetCode.

Round 3: Technical Interview

This was the most comprehensive round, focusing on my technical knowledge and projects.

What They Asked

Explanation of OOP concepts with examples (e.g., inheritance, polymorphism).

Accenture visited our campus at IET DAVV, Indore for campus recruitment. Prior to the recruitment process, students had completed the necessary formalities, including form submissions and document verification. Accenture conducted 2-3 virtual pre-placement talks before the recruitment process began. Note: A PAN card is mandatory for candidates applying to Accenture.

Round 1: Cognitive and Technical Assessment

Date: 5 September 2024
Duration: 90 minutes
Number of Questions: 90
Platform: MSB
Domains Covered: Aptitude, Logical Reasoning, Technical Questions (Cloud, Azure, MS Excel, Networking, Programming, etc.)
The results of the Cognitive Assessment were declared immediately after completing the test. The test window had a timer that refreshed every few minutes, so there was no need to worry about time management.

Round 2: Coding Assessment

After successfully completing the Cognitive and Technical Assessment, shortlisted candidates moved on to the Coding Round on the same day. This round consisted of two coding questions, both at an easy difficulty level.

Coding Questions:

Find the number of 1's in a given binary number.
Input: 1011
Output: 3
Determine which team wins in a competition based on given inputs of wins for Team A and Team B.
Input:5
TeamA
TeamB
TeamA
TeamB
TeamBOutput: TeamB
I managed to solve both questions within 5-10 minutes and successfully completed the Coding Round. After this, I received an email from Accenture confirming my successful completion of the coding assessment and providing details for the next steps.

Round 3: Communication Assessment

A few days later, shortlisted students received a link for the Communication Assessment. I completed this round on 11 September 2024. Although it was a non-elimination round, the score is included in the final evaluation. The assessment consisted of a listening and speaking test, where we had to accurately repeat words and sentences based on instructions. There was also a short summary section requiring us to give a brief summary after listening to a paragraph.

After 2-3 days, I received an email to select my interview slot, with options available from 10 AM to 4 PM in 20-minute intervals.

Round 4: Interview

Approximately 210 students were shortlisted for the final interview. My interview took place on 18 September 2024 and lasted about 15 minutes. The interview focused on project discussions and HR questions, with no technical questions asked.

Key Points from My Interview:

Project-Related Questions:Explain your best project.
What difficulties did you face while making your project, and how did you overcome them?
Discuss challenges faced in group projects.
Why did you choose to use MongoDB in your project? (Relevant to my MERN stack project on my resume.)

HR Questions:A discussion based on my resume.
Why are you proficient in C++?
What is your least favorite subject?
Do you have any questions for us?

I joined the interview lobby on the HirePro/Accenture Interview Platform about 10 minutes before my scheduled time and was fortunate to get my interviewer within 5 minutes. Some of my peers had to wait over 30 minutes for their interviews, leading to rescheduling for some on 27 September 2024.

Final Outcome

After the interview, I received an email stating that I would get the final results within 10-15 working days. The final selection for the role (ASE or AASE) was based on cumulative scores from all rounds.

On 9 October 2024, our college TNP received the final results. Out of the candidates interviewed, 68 students were shortlisted, and I was proud to be one of them. All selected students received a congratulatory email, while rejected candidates received notification emails.

Conclusion

This was my journey through the Accenture recruitment process, and I am thrilled to announce that I am officially placed in the current market scenario!

experiences.title: Accenture Interview Experience for the PADA Role
experiences.full_content:
Recently, I had the opportunity to interview for the PADA (Packaged and App Development Associate) role at Accenture. The experience was both enlightening and nerve-wracking, and I’d like to share the key aspects of the interview.

Introduction

The interview began with a warm introduction from the interviewer, who introduced himself and his role within Accenture. This initial interaction helped ease my nerves and set a positive tone for the conversation.

Self-Introduction

Following this, I was asked to introduce myself. I took this opportunity to highlight my academic background, relevant experiences, and enthusiasm for PADA and process improvement. I emphasized my interest in leveraging technology to drive business solutions, which aligns well with Accenture’s mission.

Project's impact

One of the most significant parts of the interview was when the interviewer asked me to discuss my projects in depth. I described a few key projects I had worked on during my academic career. I explained my challenges, the methodologies I employed, and the project's impact. The interviewer was particularly interested in my problem-solving approach and how I collaborated with my team to overcome obstacles.

Curriculum Insights

The conversation then shifted to my academic experience, specifically my favorite and least favorite subjects. I expressed my passion for data analytics and machine learning as my favorite areas, while also acknowledging that subjects like theoretical statistics were more challenging for me. This part of the discussion was insightful, as it showed my ability to reflect on my strengths and areas for improvement.

Team Conflicts

Next, the interviewer inquired about any conflicts I had faced while working in teams on projects. I shared a specific instance where differing opinions on project direction led to some tension. I explained how we resolved the conflict through open communication and compromise, ultimately leading to a successful project outcome. This demonstrated my ability to navigate team dynamics and contribute to a collaborative environment.

Closing Questions

As the interview was coming to a close, the interviewer asked if I had any questions. I took this opportunity to inquire about the team culture and the types of projects I might be working on in the PADA role. This not only showed my genuine interest in the position but also allowed me to gain insights into the work environment at Accenture.

Conclusion

Overall, the interview was a valuable experience that helped me better understand the role and Accenture’s expectations. I left the interview feeling positive about the interaction and hopeful about the opportunity to contribute to such a dynamic organization.

experiences.full_content:
I took part in the Accenture on-campus placement. There are 4 rounds to get selected in Accenture. Around 26 Jul 2024 the college gave me the notice and I fill up the application form. In the Application form you need to select 3 preferred job locations, so think about that in advance. A PAN Card is mandatory for taking the exam.

My Timeline was something like this:

Application form - 26 Jul 2024
1st Round: 28 Aug, 2024
2nd Round: 28 Aug, 2024
3rd Round: 30 Aug, 2024 - 1 Sep, 2024
4th Round: 5 Sep, 2024
Result : 28 Sep, 2024

1st Round: Cognitive and Technical Assessment - MCQ Test (90 Questions – 90 min):

The first round is about Cognitive and Technical Assessment. You may have to go to other colleges to take this exam. In this round there are No Quantitative Aptitude questions which makes it easier to clear this round.

In this round, there will be 90 questions from 6 sections and you will have 90 minutes. you can switch between the sections. To clear this you need to score a minimum of 75% (may change according to the cut-off).

English Ability(Verbal)

17 Ques

Critical Reasoning and Problem Solving

18 Ques

Abstract Reasoning

15 Ques

Common Application and MS Office

12 Ques

Pseudo Code

18 Ques

Fundamentals of Networking, Security, and Cloud

10 Ques

My Tip : Go to YouTube and search for these topic videos, try solve problem and practice a little. Don't take it lightly, many of my friends eliminated in this round but they are good at coding so they did not able get the chance to go to the coding round.

2nd Round: Coding Test (2 Questions – 45 min):

The Coding Test will be held on the same day if you clear round 1.

There will be 2 questions Easy/Medium level and you will have 45 minutes. The difficulty level depends on luck. Most of the time it is easy level questions. The first question will be always easy and the 2nd question may be difficult.

You need to Solve any 1 questions to clear this round.

My tip: Search for Accenture Previous year Coding questions and Most important if you find the current year questions means your previous slots questions that will be JACKPOT!!!!!! (try to find your previous days questions or that month's questions). Most of the time the same questions comes.

3rd Round: Communication Assessment:

After clearing the coding round you need take part of this Communication Assessment round. It is a Non Elimination round but you have to sit on this round mandatorily. You will have 2-3 days to complete this round.

Ensure you are in a quiet environment, as any noise could disrupt the assessment process. Speak clearly into the microphone during the assessment. Make sure your internet connection is stable. The assessment is divided into the following 6 sections:

Reading (8 ques): In this section, you will see sentences on your screen, and you will need to read them aloud with proper punctuation.
Repeat (16 ques): In this section, you will hear a few sentences, and you need to repeat each sentence exactly as you heard it. Some sentences may be in an American accent, so stay attentive.
Questions (24 ques): In this section, you will be hear several questions, and you need to provide answers based on the question. For example, if the question is, "Would you get water from a bottle or a newspaper?" you would respond, "A bottle" or "From a bottle."
Sentence Builds (10 ques): In this section, you will hear a group of words that you need to rearrange to form a proper sentence. For example, if you hear, "was reading" … "my mother" … "her favorite magazine," you would say, "My mother was reading her favorite magazine."
Story Retellings (3 ques): In this section, you will hear a brief story. You will need to remember the characters, the situation, and other important details, then retell the story as accurately as you can within 30 seconds.
Open Questions (2 ques): In this section, you will hear a question about a specific topic, and you need to speak on that topic for 40 seconds.
My tips: Search in YouTube, see how this round is conducted. Sit in a quite place with a good headphone (either 3.5mm jack or USB). I suggest to take the exam at night. Check the headphone before taking the exam.

Listen to the questions very carefully as It might be on foreign accent.

4th Round: Interview (Online):

At first, you need to book a time slot of your preference to take the interview. The Interview can start late so don't panic at that time wait in the virtual interview lobby.

Accenture generally focuses on project-based questions and HR questions, so you must have thorough knowledge of your projects and prepare some basic HR questions.

Questions that my interviewer asked me are as follows:

Introduced yourself
Have you done any team projects?
Tell me about the project.
What was your role?
What are the key learnings of the project?
What difficulties you faced during the project?
Have you ever been unsuccessful?
Why do you want to join Accenture
What is name of the CEO of Accenture?
Do you know how many employees currently work in Accenture?
Apart from studies have you done anything for society?
What is your least favorite subject in college and why?
Do you ever faced any problems with your team members?
Any questions for me?
My tips: The questions are easy and the interviewer is also friendly so Just be honest and confident and speck normally. Prepare the basic HR questions. As most of the questions come from the project so make sure you know everything about the projects. Sometimes the interviewer may asked technical questions based on your tech stack. Also prepare the core subjects like Basic DSA, OOPS, DBMS etc.

Pay close attention of what you are saying as the next question can be asked based on what you have said. One more think your selection will be based on your performance and LUCK. So don't depend on this one company, try on other companies also.

Result: Rejected

ALL THE BEST !!!

experiences.title: Accenture Interview Experience |On Campus | Advanced Application Engineer Analyst
experiences.full_content:
During an on-campus recruitment drive at my college, I had the opportunity to interview with a company that left me with a memorable experience. The entire process was structured in multiple stages, each designed to assess different skill sets, leading to my eventual success.

Stage 1: Aptitude Test

The recruitment process began with an offline aptitude test held in the digital center of my college. The test consisted of five sections:

Verbal Reasoning
Logical Reasoning
Aptitude
Abstract Reasoning
Basic Technical Questions
The final section focused on computer applications. This test was the first filter, and students who passed the eligibility criteria were able to move on to the next stage.

Stage 2: Coding Test

After clearing the aptitude test, the next stage was a coding test that lasted 45 minutes. The test included two questions:

The first question was relatively easy and meant to gauge basic coding proficiency.
The second question was more challenging, particularly for those familiar with competitive programming. It involved dynamic programming and could be classified as a "hard" level problem on most coding platforms.
Completing this round qualified me for the next stage.

Stage 3: Verbal Communication Round

The verbal communication round was non-eliminative, meaning all students who passed the coding round could participate. The purpose of this round was to assess our communication skills—an important aspect of a service-based company where client interaction is crucial.

Stage 4: Techno-Managerial Interview

The final stage of the recruitment process was a techno-managerial interview. This round began with the interviewer asking me to introduce myself, followed by a detailed discussion of one of the projects I had listed on my resume. The interviewer was curious as to why I chose to present that specific project over others.

During the discussion, I was asked about:

The tech stack I used.
The design I applied to the project.
Its practical application in a real-world scenario.
Following the technical questions, the interviewer shifted focus to behavioral questions. One key question was related to my academic background since my degree was in a field unrelated to the job I was applying for. I was asked to explain why I wanted to pursue this role despite my specialization.

The interview concluded with questions about my hobbies and interests, assessing my ability to balance technical skills with personal development. Throughout the interview, the focus remained on my ability to communicate effectively and demonstrate a clear understanding of technical concepts—a critical requirement for this service-based company.

The Result

After 10 days of waiting, I received an email informing me that I had been selected for the job! This journey taught me the importance of balancing technical proficiency with strong communication skills, especially when working in a service-oriented environment.

Tip: If you are unable to think for the optimal solution of the problem make sure you submit the brute force if that's coming to your mind.

Round 3: Communication Assessment (30 mins)

I received the link for the communication assessment on 23rd September, and I needed to complete it within 24 hours. Around 75 students got the round 3 test link (approximately 300 students appeared in round 1). I took this test from my room, as it could be attempted from anywhere. The assessment had a duration of 30 minutes and consisted of around 6 sections.

Reading (8 ques): you will see sentences on your screen, and you need to read them.
Repeat (16 ques): In this section, you will hear a few sentences, and you need to repeat each sentence exactly as you heard it. Accent of the sentence can vary (American accent).

Sentence Builds (10 ques): you will hear a group of words that you need to rearrange to form a proper sentence. For example, if you hear, “was reading” … “my mother” … “her favorite magazine,” you would say, “My mother was reading her favorite magazine.”

I joined the interview lobby at 10:30 AM (the time slot I had selected), but it showed that I was in the queue and needed to wait. My interview eventually started at 12:10 PM. The interviewer was a 15-year experienced professional from Accenture.

He asked me to show my college ID and PAN or ADHAR card.
He then introduced himself to me.
Then he asked to me introduce myself.
I mentioned one internship in my introduction, so he started asking me about that internship. He asked what you did at your intern and questions related to implementation of fuzzy search (i have worked on implementing fuzzy searching during my intern.)
He went through my resume and asked about my projects. I explained it to him, then i have discussion with him about the actual utility of the project. He asked about the project technicality.
Asked about my next project, "was it solo or group project?" ."The problem you faced while making this project".
He asked what did i do at my college club (I am in one of my college Society E-CELL).
Then He asked "What do you know about Accenture?". "Why do want to join this company?". "Why should i consider You?".
After this He told me that he is done with all the questions, Now i can ask if i have some questions for him.
I asked two question from him.. "What's the most good thing he love about working at Accenture?". "Is there any project related to AI, Machine learning in which i will get chance to work if i join Accenture?"
He replied to my questions and interview ended.

Tip: They focus mainly on projects and HR questions in the interview. Try to have good understanding of your project and read HR related questions. Be calm and try to speak normally (Not too fast) it shows your confidence and stability. Go through CS fundamentals also, sometimes they ask from that also.

Result: SELECTED (Got selection mail on 4th October midnight)

ALL THE BEST..!!
